newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen priced at $70-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen priced at $70-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Monday were seen priced at $70.00 per cwt by owners amid outlooks for firm beef prices next week, feedlot sources said.

The expectations for a rebound in beef prices overshadowed Friday's USDA monthly Cattle on Feed report, which was viewed neutral as percentages in three major report categories were near trade expectations, the sources said.

There were light sales on Friday at $67.00, steady with light sales Thursday but down $1.00 from Wednesday. Several feedlot managers said they expected prices to firm if beef prices rebound as expected.
"This thing has got a better feel to it," one feedlot manager in the Texas Panhandle said.
Fed cattle trade could be slow early next week, with several major meat packers planning production slowdowns, market sources said.
But the packers could expand production if retail beef demand increases, said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst with Alaron Trading Corp in Chicago.
"If the beef market starts to firm up, they (packers) can always increase line speeds," Levitt said.
Beef prices at Friday's close were quoted down $0.38 to up $0.14, with 417 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $0.14 at $101.93, the first increase since March 4, but is still down $5.86 in the same period, USDA statistics showed.
